hints: Focus on what acidified dichromate actually tests for, the orange to green colour change when an alcohol can be oxidised.
Look closely at the carbon carrying the OH group in each structure and count how many other carbons it is joined to.
Three of these are primary alcohols that will be oxidised, so spot the one with an OH on a fully substituted carbon that resists oxidation.
walkthrough:
**Recall the dichromate test**

Think of acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ as an oxidising agent looking for something to oxidise. If oxidation happens, you see orange to green.

$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \text{(orange)} \rightarrow \text{Cr}^{3+} \text{(green)}$$

**Link oxidation to alcohol class**

Remember the simple rule. Primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes then acids, secondary alcohols oxidise to ketones, but tertiary alcohols are not oxidised.

So only a primary or secondary alcohol will give the colour change.

**Classify A, B and C**

In A, the $\text{OH}$ is on a $\text{CH}_2$ group at the end of the chain. In B and C, the $\text{OH}$ is also on a $\text{CH}_2$ group next to a $\text{C=C}$ bond. All three are primary alcohols, $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$.

They will all be oxidised on warming, so all give orange to green.

**Classify D and conclude**

In D, the $\text{OH}$ is on a carbon joined to two methyl groups and one carbon chain. That is three carbons in total, so it is a tertiary alcohol, $\text{R}_3\text{COH}$.

It cannot be oxidised, so no colour change occurs. This is the different observation.

options.A: Incorrect. The OH is on a CH2 group, making it a primary alcohol. It is oxidised by warm acidified dichromate, giving the orange to green change like B and C.
options.B: Incorrect. The OH is on a CH2 group attached to C=C, a primary allylic alcohol. It is readily oxidised to an aldehyde then acid, so it gives the same positive result as A and C.
options.C: Incorrect. This is an isomer of B with the OH again on a CH2 group, so it is also a primary alcohol. It will be oxidised and show the orange to green change.
options.D: Correct. The OH is attached to a carbon bonded to three other carbons, so it is a tertiary alcohol. Tertiary alcohols resist oxidation by acidified K2Cr2O7, so the solution stays orange, different from the other three.
